transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Sofia Ramos (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Aurora Tech - Lead Eng), Priya Singh (Aurora - DevOps), Noah Patel (Aurora - Product), Maya Brooks (Aurora - Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): quick SDK walk through, env var, api key example, talked about dedicated and vpc, security ask for soc two and kms notes

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Jared, AE at Redwood. With me is Sofia, our SE. Today we'll do a short SDK integration walkthrough — Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth patterns, env setup, and then some recommendations for a small pilot.
[02:00] Sofia: Hi Liam, Priya, Noah, Maya — quick context check, what's your immediate goal? Is this a POC for chat features or a broader rollout?
[04:00] Liam: Mostly chat + summarization for our support flow. Latency is pretty important for us, target p95 under 300ms for short context, and we also have data isolation requirements — ideally VPC or Dedicated.
[06:00] Priya: From infra side we prefer managed hosted initially but with VPC peering for sensitive flows. Also we use KMS for key rotation, and SSO via our identity provider.
[08:00] Sofia: Got it. We'll show the quickstart. In Python it's two lines to install, then set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var. For TS same idea, npm install @redwood/sdk, then set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY or use a .env file.
[10:00] Jared: Quick note on auth: hosted API is API-key based for quickstarts. For Private you can integrate SAML/SSO and connect to their KMS for key wrapping and rotation. We also support Vault/HSM integrations for enterprise.
[12:00] Noah: When you say REDWOOD_API_KEY, is that per-service key with RBAC? We need per-route scoping for different teams.
[14:00] Sofia: Yes, keys can be scoped and you can use RBAC in the Console. For Dedicated/Private we offer SSO + RBAC and audit logs. From the quickstart, we demo a small sample:
[16:00] Speaker 1: (reading snippet) import redwood; client = redwood.Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) — this is roughly what the transcript shows, might be slightly off.
[18:00] Sofia: Right, in TypeScript it's const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' }); we recommend setting the region env var to match your latency region.
[20:00] Liam: How do we handle staging vs prod envs? Do you recommend separate projects or the same project with environment tags?
[22:00] Sofia: Many customers create separate projects for staging and prod to avoid accidental usage. You can also use route-level token scopes if you prefer a single project. We'll share a quickstart repo that shows both patterns.
[24:00] Priya: About cost — if we hit spikes, is there autoscaling for Dedicated, and is fallback to hosted available?
[26:00] Jared: Yes, Dedicated has configurable autoscaling and burst capacity options. We also provide smart routing/fallbacks so you can degrade to a cheaper model or hosted capacity if Dedicated is saturated. We discussed batching and caching — automatic prefix/KV cache reduces token costs, though our transcriptions sometimes say KV cash instead of cache, ignore that.
[28:00] Maya: Security: we need SOC 2 evidence, encryption at rest, and KMS key rotation logs. Also does Redwood provide audit logs for model calls?
[30:00] Jared: We provide audit logs in the Console with token-level tracing, and you can integrate with your SIEM. SOC 2 docs and a security pack are available; I'll send those items. For KMS, we can integrate customer-managed keys for Private deployments and Dedicated can optionally use a customer KMS.
[32:00] Sofia: For the SDK examples — here's a typical Python snippet we show in the quickstart:
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), model='redwood-v1')
resp = client.generate(prompt='Summarize recent support tickets')
print(resp.text)

There was a small mis-transcription on the deck where it said redwood-v-one, it's actually redwood-v1.
[34:00] Noah: For benchmarking, what telemetry will you need from us? We'll collect a prompt set of about 200 representative prompts and expected latency distribution.
[36:00] Sofia: Perfect. We'll run those through the hosted environment first to baseline, then Dedicated pilot on similar hardware. We'll compare p95, cost/token, and quality metrics. We'll share the benchmark spreadsheet link after the call.
[38:00] Priya: Is there a quick creds rotation example? We use automated rotation every 30 days.
[40:00] Jared: We recommend short-lived keys for hosted and automatic rotation hooks for Private. If you use customer-managed KMS, keys rotate per your KMS policies and Redwood honors those with rewrap. We'll include a section in the quickstart about rotating REDWOOD_API_KEY with KMS.
[42:00] Liam: What about SDK versions and breaking changes? How do you manage model rollouts?
[44:00] Sofia: Console supports pinned model versions and rollout policies — canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback. For SDKs we maintain changelogs and semver. Our SDK quickstart notes a pin to a specific model and client version to avoid surprises.
[46:00] Jared: Recap — action items: we'll send pricing and Dedicated options, Sofia will share quickstart repo and code snippets, customer will prepare prompt set and confirm pilot timeline.
[48:00] Maya: Also please include SOC 2, sample SAML integration doc, and KMS integration notes.
[50:00] Jared: Absolutely. We'll follow up with a single email that contains the repo link, deck, benchmark sheet, and security pack. Thanks everyone, we'll set the pilot kickoff once we get the prompt set.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker labels are mostly correct but there are a few generic labels (Speaker 1) and occasional mis-typed product names. References to KV cache sometimes transcribed as "KV cash".
